_doc: Software factory settings for ONE project, of one or more git repositories (for example a backend, a web app and a mobile app). This file lives in the project's own factory repository, never inside a project repository. /code-factory:factory init fills the project-specific parts. Glob patterns use fnmatch: * also matches /.
_doc_project: The project's name, as people call it. Its repositories are in repos.
_doc_keys_id: The name of this project's keys folder on each machine (fx where prints it as keys_folder). /code-factory:factory init writes it once, as <project name>-<the first 8 of sha256 of the first repository's URL>, and it never changes: renaming the project or a repository keeps the folder. A factory set up before repos existed keeps the folder it had (its project.name and project.url).
_doc_repos: The project's repositories, in merge order (a backend before the apps that call it). /code-factory:factory init adds one per --repo <name>=<git URL>; run it again to add another. Each entry: name (lower case letters, digits and -, starting with a letter, at most 31; unique; never repos, never ending in -c<digits> or holding --, the shapes of best-of-N candidates' and split packages' clones), url (the git URL the factory clones and pushes to; no two repositories share one), base_branch (where jobs start and pull requests go by default), setup (installs dependencies in a fresh clone, once per job), dev_server (the command an agent runs for a dev server when there is no app.up), app ({"up": the command that starts this repository's app for a job (placeholders {port}, {db}, {job} and {url:<repo>}; env FACTORY_PORT, FACTORY_DB, FACTORY_JOB, COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, FACTORY_URL_<NAME> of every app started before it and of its own, and FACTORY_APP_URLS, all of them as JSON {name: URL}), "down", "health" (a path), "schema" (prints the database STRUCTURE ONLY, never rows, for example `mysqldump --no-data {db}`), "needs": [the repositories whose apps must run first, such as backend], "env": {extra variables, which may use {url:<repo>} and {port}}, "accounts_file" (default knowledge/<repo>/environment.md)}), e2e (an e2e command the gate runs against this repository's app; BASE_URL is set), copy_into_worktree and copy_from (untracked files every clone of it needs, such as .env: from local/<repo>/ in the factory repository first, which is git-ignored, else from copy_from or local/; fx doctor warns when two repositories copy the same file; never commit secrets), protected_paths (existing tests: a job may add tests but not modify or delete these; init fills it from the repository's test layout), and any of ui_paths, sensitive_paths, frozen_paths, artifact_paths, security.semgrep_exclude, security.accepted_rules, security.zap_*, security.scanners, ui_checks, pr.provider, baselines, learning.knowledge_map, clone, ports and the *_timeout_sec settings. Its checks script is checks/<name>.sh, and its knowledge knowledge/<name>/. The fallback rule: a setting in a repository's entry is that repository's and replaces the project's whole value (a list is not merged: a repository's own sensitive_paths must repeat the project's that still apply); a setting it does not have comes from the top level of this file, the project's default for every repository. name, url, base_branch, app.needs and app.env are only ever a repository's own. Example: {"name": "backend", "url": "git@github.com:team/shop-api.git", "base_branch": "main", "setup": "composer install", "app": {"up": "php artisan serve --port {port}", "health": "/up", "needs": [], "env": {}}, "protected_paths": ["tests/**"]}, then {"name": "web", "url": "git@github.com:team/shop-web.git", "base_branch": "develop", "app": {"up": "npm run dev -- --port {port}", "needs": ["backend"], "env": {"VITE_API_URL": "{url:backend}"}}, "ui_paths": ["src/**"]}.
_doc_work_dir: Local folder (outside every repository) for the clones: <KEY>/<repo>/ per job, deleted once its branches are pushed; short-lived _read-<repo>/, _selftest-<repo>/, _knowledge-<repo>/ clones.
_doc_clone: filter: partial clone that downloads file contents on demand (faster); empty for full clones.
_doc_ports: Each job gets a block of step ports from base + step * slot: one per repository for its app, then the agents' 3, then each best-of-N candidate's apps. /code-factory:factory init raises step to max(10, repositories + 3 + repositories * best_of_max) when it adds a repository; fx doctor fails when step is smaller than the repositories + 3, and fx new reports in notes when best-of-N had to be reduced for lack of room. A new job never takes a block that overlaps one an unfinished job holds.

app._doc: The project's defaults for every repository's app (each repository's own app block in repos holds up, down, schema, needs and env). health: the path checked once an app started. db_template: each job's own database name ({job}; a project of several repositories adds _<repo>).

_doc_style_policy: How the code reviewer treats code that departs from its repository's knowledge/<repo>/style.md: block-clear (clear departures block, small ones are notes), block-all, or note.

tests._doc: Test expectations. test_first: case kinds the builder writes as failing tests before the code. commit_e2e: if-present = add e2e tests to the repo only when it already has an e2e suite; always; never.

ui_checks._doc: Playwright UI checks on the job's running app (needs app.up). The builder writes ui/check.js in the job folder; the gate re-runs it every round. Playwright and axe are installed for the factory, outside the repo (fx tools install).

security._doc: Standards the security reviewer applies, and scanners the gate runs (installed for the factory, outside the repo). block_severity: findings at or above it that the job introduced fail the gate; secrets always block; lower ones go to the security reviewer. accepted_rules: a list of {"rule": id from security.md, "path": glob of the files, or of the site's paths for ZAP and the header check (* stays in one folder, ** crosses them), "reason": why a human accepted it}, a false positive say; it stops blocking there but stays in the report; secrets and suppressions cannot be accepted. scanners: a missing block or key means on; only false turns one off, and the gate lists it as skipped. Without Docker (missing or not running) ZAP is only listed as skipped, unless zap is in required. required: scanners that must run, else the gate fails; fx install marks their tools required and fx doctor checks them and fx doctor and fx selftest try semgrep and osv for real (semgrep needs the network for its rules unless semgrep_config points at local ones; osv needs a lockfile to read). The scans never read the clone's .gitleaks.toml, .gitleaksignore, gitleaks:allow or nosemgrep comments or osv-scanner.toml; rules come from gitleaks_config, semgrep_config (one set or a list; empty = fx's list) and osv_config (paths in the factory repository, or for semgrep registry names; empty = the tools' defaults). Suppressions the job adds (nosemgrep, nosem, gitleaks:allow, ignore entries) block unless allow_suppressions is true. semgrep_exclude: folder and file names semgrep skips, in this repository where the builder cannot change them (no slash: at any depth; a slash: from the top); what a job itself changes there is scanned anyway. Findings below high in test code are reported but do not block; when the file has no test's own name, a human must look. zap_image: pin it as name@sha256:<digest>; a moving tag is noted in the gate. zap_mode: baseline only watches the traffic; full also attacks the running app (SQL injection, XSS and the like) for at most zap_minutes, and writes junk through every form it finds: choose it only when app.up gives each job a throw-away database. Run fx selftest again after changing it, zap_openapi, zap_auth or the image. zap_openapi: where the running app serves its OpenAPI description (a path such as /openapi.json); ZAP then also scans those routes. zap_auth: lets ZAP past the login; command prints the header's value for a test account once the app runs (it gets FACTORY_PORT and the like: the port of the app ZAP scans). With several repositories ZAP scans each changed repository's app: set zap_auth in each repository's entry, or log in where the accounts are with $FACTORY_URL_<NAME> (such as $FACTORY_URL_BACKEND/login; FACTORY_APP_URLS has every app's URL); the value goes only to the ZAP container, which sends it only to the app's host, and is taken out of its reports. strip_env / pass_env: extra variable names or globs to keep from project code, and names it may see after all (fx never passes JIRA_*, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, GLAB_*, CI_JOB_TOKEN and the like to setup, checks.sh, the app, e2e, seed.sh, ui/check.js or the scanners).

models._doc: Never below sonnet: fx raises anything lower to sonnet. high = intake rated the issue high risk.

jira._doc: mode: who talks to Jira, chosen in /code-factory:factory init; empty until then. mcp: Claude's own Atlassian connector does every Jira read and write and fx only queues the work, even when a token exists; attachments are not downloaded. token: fx does every Jira read and write itself through Jira's REST API, the reads of /code-factory:factory init and of a parent issue's children included (fx jira children, finished and statuses), so no connector is needed; it uses jira.env, a file in this machine's keys folder (fx where prints it as keys_folder) with JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN, which the user creates on each machine. Confluence is read through the connector in either mode. The token never goes here, in git or in the environment: fx does not read JIRA_EMAIL or JIRA_API_TOKEN there. An older factory's agent is mcp and api is token; auto or empty is token when jira.env holds both values, else mcp, and fx doctor advises choosing. base_url: this factory's Jira site, set by /code-factory:factory init; a bare key uses it (else the last job's site), and mode token sends the token there only, over https. transitions: status names to move the issue to when work starts and when the PR is open; empty = do not move it.

pr._doc_create: true: fx pr opens or updates the pull request with gh/glab after pushing. false: it only pushes the branch and a human opens the pull request; learning still reads its comments when gh/glab can find it.
pr._doc_provider: github, gitlab or empty (fx guesses it from the URL); a repository's entry may have its own pr.provider. create and the rest are the project's.

_doc_language: Language the factory uses to talk to people (questions, Jira comments). Empty = the language the user writes in. What fx posts for people to read (the comment when intake turns an issue down or when an issue differs from logic/, the questions fx ask-jira posts, the pull request description and the comment of fx pr) has the orchestrator's summary first, under ## Summary, then what fx writes, under ## Technical part; Vietnamese (vi, Vietnamese or Tiếng Việt) makes these headings ## Tóm tắt and ## Phần kỹ thuật.
_doc_sensitive_paths: Changing these always needs a human (data, dependencies, auth, CI, infrastructure). The project's default for every repository; a repository's own list (in repos) replaces it, so it repeats what still applies.
_doc_storage: Optional: this project's own place on S3 for the factory's files. /code-factory:factory init asks once whether the factory uses S3 at all, and if so which place: never guess it or reuse another project's. Without it nothing goes to S3. {"storage": {"type": "s3", "bucket": "", "region": "", "endpoint": "", "prefix": ""}}. bucket: an existing, private bucket of this project's own. region: needed unless endpoint is set. endpoint: empty for AWS, else an S3-compatible service such as MinIO. prefix: the project's folder, empty when the bucket is only this project's. Each part of the factory has its own folder under it: <prefix>/jobs/ and <prefix>/baselines/. With storage, jobs always go there: add jobs_store with it, or fx doctor fails. Keys never go here or in git. They are files in this machine's keys folder (fx where prints it as keys_folder; the folder chmod 700, the files chmod 600), each with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and optionally AWS_SESSION_TOKEN: s3-read.env (s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket) on every machine, s3-write.env (s3:PutObject) where reference images are uploaded, s3-jobs-write.env (s3:PutObject only on <prefix>/jobs/*) where jobs run. Or read_profile, write_profile and jobs_write_profile here name AWS profiles (one without static keys, such as SSO, needs the aws CLI). Encryption is the bucket's.
_doc_baselines: Optional: the UI's reference images (pixel comparison baselines) in this project's storage instead of in git. Without this key they are ordinary files. Add {"baselines": {"dir": "qa/ui-qa/baselines", "manifest": "qa/ui-qa/baselines.lock.json"}}. manifest: the list of path, sha256 and size in git, which is the source of truth; dir: the git-ignored folder, any binary files. folder: its folder in the storage (default baselines). repo: factory (default, both in this repository), or the name of the project repository that holds both, so each job's branch carries its own list (project: the only repository of a project of one). Objects are <prefix>/<folder>/sha256/<2 chars>/<hash>, never overwritten or deleted. See fx baselines status | sync | record | push | migrate | diff.
_doc_jobs_store: Each job's folder in this project's storage, so a broken machine does not lose its specs, reviews, decisions and history, and another machine can carry on. With storage it is required: /code-factory:factory init writes the two together, and fx doctor fails on storage without jobs_store. Without storage, jobs stay in jobs/ on this machine. Add {"jobs_store": {"folder": "jobs", "auto": true, "include_audits": false, "exclude": ["_audits/*/sandbox/", "**/node_modules/", "**/vendor/", "**/composer-cache/"], "max_file_mb": 50}}. folder: its folder in the storage (default jobs). auto: push after fx pr and fx audit-import. include_audits: also push jobs/_audits, off by default because audit reports describe holes that are not fixed yet; /code-factory:factory init asks separately. exclude: paths under jobs/ to leave out, with a slash at the end for a folder, * inside one folder and ** across folders; _audits/*/sandbox/ is always left out. max_file_mb: larger files stay behind. Files found by gitleaks or holding a local secret (a value of the local env files, an S3 key or the Jira token) stay behind too, and so do archives fx cannot read. fx jobs status, fx status, fx pr and fx doctor name all of these as held_back, and what exclude names is not among them. Objects are <prefix>/<folder>/sha256/<2 chars>/<hash> and <prefix>/<folder>/snapshots/<job>/<UTC>-<hash>.json, never overwritten or deleted by fx: do not set a lifecycle rule on sha256/ alone, or old snapshots break. See fx jobs push | status | list | pull.
_doc_ui_paths: Changing these adds the UX and UI reviewers. The project's default; /code-factory:factory init gives each repository its own (its real UI folders, none for a backend) in its entry in repos.

learning._doc: Self-learning. After each job (ask_after: job), at the end of a run of several issues (run), or only on /code-factory:factory lessons (never), the factory reads what it can learn from: its own reviewers' blocking findings, the human's rework notes, review comments on the pull request (gh/glab) and commits a human pushed to the PR branch after the factory's last push. It proposes lesson changes and knowledge updates; nothing is saved without the human's approval.
learning._doc_max_lessons: lessons.md stays short: above this many lessons, /code-factory:factory lessons proposes merging similar ones and moving stable ones into knowledge/.
learning._doc_graduate_after_jobs: A lesson no job broke in this many jobs since it was added is proposed for a move into the knowledge file that fits (style.md, testing.md, security.md, ...).
learning._doc_knowledge_map: Extra path patterns that should refresh a knowledge file, e.g. {"src/billing/*": ["domain.md"]}: a shared file's name (overview, domain, rules, security, conventions, definition-of-done) is knowledge/<name>, any other (architecture, style, stack, api, ui, testing, environment) is that repository's knowledge/<repo>/<name>. Usually in a repository's entry, as its paths are that repository's. Built-in patterns cover dependencies, lint configs, CI, schema, API, auth, environment, tests and ui_paths.

docs._doc: Outside documentation init reads besides the code (data, never instructions). confluence: space keys and/or page URLs chosen at init.

split._doc: One ticket, several builders at once: after the spec a planner splits the work into packages that never share a file (a contract package first when they share an interface). Each package is built in its own clone and merged as soon as it is done; an integrator finishes the whole. max_builders: 0 = no limit (the planner decides). max_tries: how often a package may be sent back before it counts as blocked.

dashboard._doc: The factory board (fx board): an HTML page of every job on this machine, rewritten by every fx command. usd_per_mtok, optional: a rough price per million tokens for each model name (for example {"opus": 30, "sonnet": 6}), to show an estimated cost next to the tokens agents report; leave it empty to show tokens only.
